2 A. INTRODUCTION This guide is meant to provide basic safety procedures for responding to emergencies in the workplace. These procedures are designed to minimize injury and loss of human life and to protect resources by providing training and guidance to employees. You are encouraged to review and understand the procedures outlined in this booklet. If you terminate or are transferred away from your office, please leave this book at your desk. B. STATEMENT OF PURPOSE This Emergency and Crisis Response Manual has been prepared in an effort to ensure emergency situations at Idaho Public Television will be responded to effectively. The goals of this manual are to: • Provide a line-of-authority roster of employees at Idaho Public Television, • Provide emergency and evacuation procedures, • Provide information so adequate action can be taken in the event of an emergency, and • Establish a business resumption plan.

3 C. LINE OF AUTHORITY In all emergency situations, immediately notify the general manager or designee. The general manager or designee will oversee overall coordination and all decision-making in the process of responding to and recovering from emergency situations. The general manager or designee will relay timely and appropriate information to the State Board of Education, the license holder. Depending on the nature of the emergency, personnel will be notified if they are to report to an alternate location.

WHEN TO GET HELP Call 911 if conditions arise that seem to have the potential to be harmful or threatening to the employees of any state office or to the building and its contents. When reporting an emergency, be prepared to supply the emergency agency with the following information: • You are calling from Idaho Public Television. • The physical address and telephone of your location: • The nature of the emergency. Do not hang up. Let the emergency personnel end the conversation. They may have more questions or important information to pass on. Notify the General Manager immediately. If he/she cannot be contacted, notify the next person on the Line of Authority list (Pages 4–5). When going to remote locations, text phones are available to be checked out. Some possible conditions to call 911 could be: • Fire • Bomb threat • Security violations • Occupied elevators “stuck” between floors

# Page 11^page=11
9 or other elevator emergencies • Unauthorized persons entering a space or premises • Disruptive person and/or suspicious activity • Theft • Evidence of illegal entry • Suspicious package is received • Natural disaster Help protect everyone’s safety: Stay alert to the conditions around you and report all unusual conditions. E. MEDICAL EMERGENCIES Call 911 Provide the following information: 1. The building name and address 2. Floor and room number 3. Type of injury (stroke, extreme pain, etc.) Have someone go to the lobby/entrance of the building to guide emergency responders to your location. REMEMBER: Emergency personnel are on their way. Remain with the injured person so that you can provide information to the responding emergency personnel. If needed, first aid kits and AEDs are available in all IdahoPTV locations.

10 F. EMERGENCY EVACUATION PROCEDURES 1. Do not use elevators. 2. Exit building by way of the safest and quickest route. Staff should familiarize themselves with the appropriate floor plans before an emergency occurs. Staff should instruct guests to exits. 3. After exiting the building, IdahoPTV staff and guests will proceed to the designated meeting area and remain there until all staff and guests are accounted for: • Boise: north side of the state DEQ building. • Moscow: west side of the parking lot. • Pocatello: southeast side of the Liberal Arts building to the Quad. 4. Do not re-enter the buildings until instructed to do so by emergency personnel. G. DESIGNATED MEETING AREA BY LOCATION • Boise: north side of the state DEQ building. • Moscow: west side of the parking lot. • Pocatello: southeast side of the Liberal Arts building to the Quad. H. EVACUATION FOR THOSE WITH DISABILITIES The human resources staff and the department supervisor shall work with the person who has a disability to provide them a primary and secondary assistant in case of an emergency. In the case of an emergency evacuation, one of the assigned assistants will meet up with the disabled person to assist with evacuation.

# Page 13^page=13
11 I. BOMB THREATS Bomb threats can be delivered in many different ways, such as by recording, email, text, or letter. The most common method used to deliver a threat is by phone. If a bomb threat is received, remain calm and immediately notify the Line of Authority. DO NOT announce the threat, as this can create panic. Two reasons that a person will call in a bomb threat are: 1. The caller is the person who placed the device or they have gained knowledge that there is a bomb in the building. The caller may want to minimize personal injury or property damage loss. 2. The caller wants to create anxiety and panic to disrupt normal activities or possibly make people move to the location of the device. The person receiving the threat should utilize the bomb threat checklist provided on Page 12. Obtaining and recording this information may help in locating the bomb, and will at least give important and useful information to authorities. After the information is obtained, the Line of Authority will seek help as per procedures (Page 3, Section C). IMPORTANT: SAVE ALL WRITTEN OR ELECTRONIC MATERIAL. IF A LETTER OR NOTE IS RECEIVED. DO NOT HAND IT AROUND, AS THIS MAY CONTAMINATE POSSIBLE EVIDENCE. IdahoPTV telephone tracing records should be made available to emergency personnel.

# Page 15^page=15
13 EVACUATION PROCESS FOR BOMB THREAT 1. The decision to evacuate should be based upon either an assumed threat or credible threat and decided by the Line of Authority or emergency authority. 2. Avoid words such as “bomb,” “explosion,” “blow up,” etc. Use instead: “Please clear the building immediately, we have an emergency.” This will reduce the possibility of panic. 3. Follow the emergency evacuation procedures (Page 10, Section F) and report to the designated meeting area. 4. People may take their personal belongings (if they are easy to access). This will make it easier for searchers to locate a possible explosive device. 5. While evacuating, observe your surroundings for anything that is out of place and for suspicious packages, and report the location to emergency personnel. J. EVACUATION PROCESS FOR EXPLOSIONS 1. Immediately take cover under desks, tables, or other objects that can provide cover from flying glass and debris. 2. After the explosion, call 911. 3. Evacuate the building using emergency evacuation procedures (Page 10, Section F).

# Page 16^page=16
14 4. Do not re-enter the building until instructed to do so by emergency personnel. K. ELEVATOR DURING EVACUATION PROCESS 1. If you are in an elevator when a fire alarm sounds, the elevator will automatically return to the ground floor. Do not push the emergency stop switch when this happens. 2. Do not attempt to use the elevator in the event of a fire alarm, as they may not be operating. L. EARTHQUAKES If you are indoors: 1. DO NOT RUN TO THE OUTDOORS. Most injuries during earthquakes occur when people try to exit a building. 2. IMMEDIATELY take shelter under desks, tables, or other objects that will provide protection from falling debris such as glass, electrical wires, etc. 3. Wait for the Line of Authority to give instructions before leaving cover. There may still be some aftershocks that could cause material to fall. 4. When it is determined that evacuation is necessary, follow the emergency evacuation procedures (Page 10, Section F). 5. Do not re-enter the building until instructed to do so by emergency personnel.

# Page 17^page=17
15 If you are outside, get into the open and away from buildings and power lines. If you are driving, stop if it is safe, but stay inside your car. Stay away from bridges, overpasses, and tunnels. Move your car as far out of the normal traffic pattern as possible. If possible, avoid stopping under trees, light posts, power lines, or signs. If you are in a mountainous area or near unstable slopes or cliffs, be alert for falling rock and other debris that could be loosened by the earthquake. M. ACTIVE SHOOTER In the event of an active shooter, overly aggressive employee, or aggressive citizen, you must be able to analyze the situation and take the most appropriate action possible. Although emergency personnel will arrive quickly, the event itself can be over by the time most agencies can stop the threat. Pre-planning is key to evading the threat posed by the aggressive person. Using the Avoid, Deny, and Defend (ADD) strategy will give an employee an advantage in this situation. AVOID: Get away from the threat and exit the building if possible. Below is a basic list on how to avoid a threat. 1. Pay attention to your surroundings. 2. Have multiple exit plans/know where the exits are. 3. Move away from the threat as quickly as possible. 4. Exit the building when safe to do so.

# Page 18^page=18
16 5. Find cover or a solid object that not only hides you but provides protection. DENY: This option is for when you cannot get away from the threat or they are blocking the way out of the building. 1. Keep distance between you and the threat. 2. Go in a room and lock the door and then continue to build a barrier with whatever you have in the room. 3. Turn off the lights. 4. Silence your phones/turn off the vibration mode. 5. Hide behind large objects, not under them. 6. Do not restrict your options for movement. 7. Continue to find a way out if possible. DEFEND: This is the last option to use. Remember: you have a right to protect yourself and others. 1. Be prepared to defend yourself. 2. Be aggressive and committed to your actions. 3. Do not fight fair or worry about hurting the threat. 4. This is about survival: throw things, yell, and work as a team.

# Page 19^page=19
17 WHEN EMERGENCY PERSONNEL ARRIVE: 1. Keep your hands visible. 2. Follow all commands given by emergency personnel, even if you think they are unreasonable. 3. Emergency personnel can be in uniform or they may be identified by a badge, whether on their belt or around their neck. 4. Do not hold onto or follow emergency personnel when they are moving toward the threat to stop it. N. TERRORIST ATTACK & WEAPONS OF MASS DESTRUCTION When an IdahoPTV employee becomes aware of a terrorist attack or weapons of mass destruction, the Line of Authority will be immediately notified. In response to a terrorist attack, IdahoPTV should be prepared to: 1. Reduce operations to a minimum. 2. Coordinate all actions with local authorities. 3. Consider the possible removal of essential equipment or elements of IdahoPTV.

# Page 20^page=20
18 O. BOISE BUILDING AND ELEVATOR LOCKDOWN When emergency personnel inform Idaho Public Television of a situation that requires the building to be locked down, the front desk staff will contact the general manager and if necessary, another person on the Line of Authority list. The general manager may contact the facilities manager to lock the front doors. They will also contact DEQ Boise Regional Office to let their staff know about the situation. If needed, they will lock down the elevator. When emergency personnel inform Idaho Public Television that the lockdown situation has ended, the front desk staff will return the elevator to the working mode. P. NOTIFYING OTHERS IN THE BUILDING DEQ – First Floor Front Desk: 208-373-0550 Scenarios and who to contact during situations (Boise focused): • An elevated conversation is taking place in the first floor lobby. • Contact Line of Authority. • Contact DEQ to inform them of the situation. • Visitor in the IdahoPTV lobby on the second floor acts agitated and conversation is elevated. • Page “Mr. Black, you have a visitor.” The

# Page 21^page=21
19 designated staff will respond and arrive at the reception desk to help defuse the situation. • Other staff who overhear or are in the area could assist by making additional telephone calls to the Line of Authority or 911. • Conversation on the telephone becomes elevated. • Control the conversation politely and let them know you will pass along the information. • Contact Line of Authority. • Caller on the telephone threatens harm to an employee. • Immediately contact Line of Authority. • Emergency personnel call and ask that we lock down the building. • Page the building to stay inside and don’t let strangers enter the building. • Send email to all staff informing them of the situation: idptvstaff@idahoptv.org • An email is received that is threatening or questionable. • Immediately contact Line of Authority.

# Page 22^page=22
20 These are primarily suggested procedures and may change based on security equipment available. Q. SUSPICIOUS PACKAGES If mail is received that is threatening or questionable, notify the Line of Authority. Keep in mind that an explosive or other life-threatening items (razor blades, anthrax) can be enclosed in either a parcel or an envelope, and its outward appearance is limited only by the imagination of the sender. However, suspicious packages have exhibited some unique characteristics that might assist you. To apply these factors, it is important to know the type of mail normally received by your department. THINGS TO LOOK FOR: • Suspicious packages might bear restricted endorsements such as “personal” or “private.” This is important when the addressee does not normally receive personal mail at the office. • The addressee’s name/title might be inaccurate. • Suspicious packages or articles might reflect distorted handwriting, or the name and address might be prepared with homemade labels or cut-and-paste lettering. • Suspicious packages or articles might have protruding wires, aluminum foil, or oil stains visible, and might emit a peculiar odor.

# Page 23^page=23
21 • Suspicious packages or articles might have an excessive amount of postage. • Letter bombs might feel rigid or appear uneven or lopsided. • Suspicious packages or articles might be unprofessionally wrapped with several combinations of tape used to secure the package and might be endorsed “Fragile- Handle With Care” or “Rush-Do Not Delay.” • Suspicious packages or articles might have an irregular shape, soft spots, or bulges. • Suspicious packages or articles might make a buzzing or ticking noise or sloshing sound. • Pressure or resistance might be noted when removing contents from an envelope or parcel. IF YOU DISCOVER A SUSPICIOUS PACKAGE OR LETTER AND ARE UNABLE TO VERIFY THE ADDRESSEE OR SENDER: • Do not take a chance. • Immediately contact the Line of Authority or 911 (depending on the level of emergency). • Do not move, alter, open, examine, or disturb the article. • Do not put it in water or a confined space such as a desk drawer or filing cabinet. • Isolate the suspicious package or article. • If 911 has been contacted: • Page the building, “Please evacuate the building immediately.”

# Page 24^page=24
22 • Inform DEQ of the situation as you are exiting the building. Or, call DEQ when you are safely outside. R. IDAHOPTV BUSINESS RESUMPTION PLAN KAID-TV BOISE AREA IdahoPTV’s Network Operations Center has back-up power generation capacity to allow for 72 hours run time without commercial power available. If the studio facilities of KAID-TV become inoperable, there are two plans for resuming a broadcast signal: 1. Equip and utilize the Capitol Mall studio to generate the necessary broadcast service and transmit signals to the Deer Point transmitter site. 2. Utilize KTVB studio and broadcast facilities. OTHER SCENARIOS In the event of a widespread emergency, such as a failure of a major utility or telecommunication network failure, IdahoPTV could provide live television broadcast of critical information to the citizens of the state from its studios assuming there is power at our studio and to our transmission sites. IdahoPTV maintains a two-way video system that links Moscow, Boise, and Pocatello together that could be used for basic point-to-point communication or for broadcast purposes. IdahoPTV is also connected by a

# Page 25^page=25
23 two-way video system that links all of the state’s higher education centers together. Each supervisor with common use equipment will make known to their staff procedures for cleaning the equipment. Appropriate supplies will be made available throughout the buildings to prevent the spread of contagious illnesses. In the event of a reduced workforce due to contagious illnesses/pandemic, flu, etc., each department will utilize their Continuity of Operations plan. In the event a portion of an IdahoPTV facility becomes unfit to occupy due to air quality, allergens, etc., the general manager or designee will assign alternate work locations whether in the facility or off-site. See IdahoPTV Return to the Workspace Guidelines on Share (share.idahoptv.org) for additional information.
